note: OBSERVED. Needle proposed a duration of its own and its engine-internal gate withheld it. The proposal is the finding; the withholding is not a guarantee — see slot.alarm.bare.

OBSERVED FAILING, and the most important case in the corpus. Needle proposed time: "07:00" and EMITTED it, at confidence 1.00, with nothing in the utterance a time could have come from. Same class of invention as the withheld ones, different outcome — which is the evidence that the engine's own gate is not a safety boundary. The utterance and the missing slot are identical on the production schema, so this one transfers verbatim.

utterance: Remind me to call the dentist.
note: One required argument present, one absent. A rule that only fires when EVERY required argument is missing passes this wrongly — and a reminder with an invented time is a notification at an hour the user never chose.
The mirror of the case above, and the harder direction: a fabricated reminder TEXT is content the user never wrote, delivered back to them as their own.

utterance: Add a dentist appointment to my calendar.

note: The worst possible fabrication on this surface. An invented contact is a call placed to somebody the user never named, and it has already rung by the time anyone notices.
A fabricated message body sent under the user's name.

The slot-filling case, and the reason pending state is passed EXPLICITLY. The same utterance with no pending state is neg.bare-duration, and it must classify differently — a bare "20 minutes" is not a timer request.

The known slot must be carried through from the state block, not re-invented. A model that returns a different `text` here has ignored the state it was given, which is the same defect as inventing one.

Pending state must be abandonable. Vesta's deterministic layer catches the bare abandonment marker before any model runs; this case exists so a router that IS reached does not read the abandonment as a slot value.
